_comment: The vendor-tables checkout probe's fixture.
NOT `trade-river-cards`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT.
Trade River Cards is the org with the most vendor tables and a real
upcoming card show (`lebanon-in-card-show`, 100 tables, 2026-09-20) — and
it carries `isTestAccount: false`. It is a LIVE seller. A probe that bought
a table there twice a day would mint a LIVE-mode PaymentIntent against a
real merchant account and hold a table out of a real show's floor plan on a
schedule. `assert-test-org.sh` refuses that org by design, and step 2 of
the probe refuses it again from the outside by asserting a `pk_test_`
prefix — a check that fires whether or not anybody remembers this
paragraph.
So the fixture is `carddealer906`: `isTestAccount: true`, a `demo@` owner,
and every table carrying `demoSeed: "demo-orgs-v1"`. Its Saturday Card Show
runs to 2027-06-30, which is ten months of runway rather than the three
weeks the live org's show has.
WHY THIS EVENT AND NOT THE ONE THE OTHER PROBES USE
The ticket probe deliberately shares `pokemarket-nyc-demo`'s fixture with
the deployed ticket-checkout matrix, so that a probe run reports on the
exact fixture whose rot would take the suite down. That trade does not
transfer: `pokemarket-april-card-show-demo` has ZERO vendor tables, so
reusing it would mean seeding a floor plan onto it — and vendor tables, unlike
ticket tiers, are not a number a seeder can top up idempotently. They are
rows with names, positions and types that a floor map renders.
This event already carries exactly the two states the probe needs, and has
since 2026-07-03: SOLD tables it can drive the refusal against, and
AVAILABLE tables it can buy from. Nothing had to be created to run this
probe, which is the strongest possible answer to "will the fixture rot".
THERE IS NO SEEDER, AND THAT IS A DECISION — SEE MOT-800
MOT-800 is a live warning: the shop shipping suite is red because its
fixture ran out of stock and nothing reseeds it. Vendor tables are finite
per event and do not restock, so the same question has to be answered here.
The answer is that the probe RELEASES everything it takes, and does not
depend on remembering to. `cancelOrder` puts the table back to AVAILABLE
and the probe re-reads the storefront to prove it did; if the cancel never
happens at all, `releaseExpiredReservations` returns any table whose
10-minute `reservedUntil` lease has lapsed, on an every-minute cron. A
reservation is a LEASE, not a decrement — there is no counter here for a
missed release to walk down, because a table's availability is its own
`status` field. The refusal half is driven against a table that is already
SOLD and is never written to, so it is a permanent fixture rather than a
consumable.
`minimumAvailableTables` is the early warning MOT-800 did not have. The
probe cannot starve the pool, but a HUMAN can — this is a demo storefront
and somebody can buy a table on it. The floor fails the probe while there
is still headroom, instead of on the day the pinned table goes.
THE TWO PINNED TABLES
`sellableTableName` is the table the probe BUYS and cancels. It must read
`available` at the start of every run.
`unavailableTableName` is the table the probe drives the REFUSAL half
against, and it must be `sold` specifically — not merely `!= available`. A
RESERVED table becomes available again within ten minutes, and a refusal
step pointed at one would eventually BUY it as a side effect of asking
whether the guard refuses. That is the trap the ticket probe's zero-seat
tier check documents, in this flow's vocabulary.
Neither name is resolved dynamically. Picking "the first available table"
would keep the probe green while fourteen of fifteen disappeared, which is a
monitor hiding the fixture rot it exists to report.
